raw_segments.text: Macbeth, thou art too like the spirit of Banquo, Down thy crown does sear mine eyeballs,
And thy hair thou other gold-bound brow is like the first,
A third is like the former. Filthy hags, why do you show me this? A fourth, start eyes,
What will the line stretch out to th, crack of doom, another yet? A seventh, I'll see
no more. And yet the eighth appears, Who bears a glass which shows me many more,
And some I see that two-fold balls and treble scepters carry.
Horrible sight, now I see teas true, For the blood-boltered Banquo smiles upon me
And points at them for his. What is this so?
